reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) shows DCT improved strength and ductility in a different BCC HEA (HfNbTaTiZr), but the hypothesis extends this to NbZrTiHfMo without evidence that the mechanism (phase transition, stress relief) operates in the presence of high Mo or addresses the specific electronegativity issue. The key premises about Mo-related embrittlement relief and transferability are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) can improve plasticity in BCC refractory high-entropy alloys.
DCT induces phase transitions or microstructural refinement that enhance dislocation mobility.
The mechanism observed in HfNbTaTiZr will transfer to the NbZrTiHfMo system despite its high Mo content.
DCT can relieve internal stresses or embrittlement caused by high electronegativity differences.
